next_step: Agree SLO definitions + start 2-week POC load test
notes:
Summary: Boreal Ops is a tier-1 telecom operator evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer chat and personalization reranking. Primary evaluation axis is latency SLO definition and measurement alignment across streaming and non-streaming traffic; second axis is reserved GPU planning and throughput guarantees.

Key constraints / asks (from CTO + Performance team):
- Absolute p95 targets for non-streaming generation: <=200ms (goal), p99 <=400ms. p50 target <=50-80ms.
- Streaming flows: initial-token p50 ~50-80ms, p95 <=250ms; steady-state chunking latency acceptable up to 100ms per chunk but p99 needs attention.
- Client-side perceived latency must match server-side telemetry for SLAs. We require deterministic measurement method before legal signs reserved contract.
- Throughput profile: 10k concurrent conversational sessions, avg 3 tokens/sec per session, burst allowance x2 for peak events.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to 12-month reserved capacity if SLOs show 30-40% improvement over current in-house infra.

Measurement alignment issues surfaced in discovery call:
- Client-side timers include network RTT and SDK batching delays; server-side timings currently measure 'inference-start' to 'inference-end' only. Need unified definitions.
- Streaming SDK reports per-chunk timestamps; Redwood runtime reports per-token times. How to produce a single p95/p99 value?
- Clock skew: mobile clients unsynchronized; recommendation needed for server-side authoritative metrics and how to include edge-to-edge latency in external SLA.

Proposed SLO definitions (drafted during SE workshop):
- Non-streaming (sync) SLOs: measure end-to-end server-to-client response time at the edge ingress proxy (server_observed_end_to_end). Use p50/p95/p99 on request-level total time including queuing. Define: p95 <=200ms, p99 <=450ms for initial evaluation.
- Server-inference-only metric: inference_duration (model execution) reported p95 <=120ms; used for capacity sizing but not for external SLA.
- Streaming SLOs: split into initial-response latency (time to first token) and steady-state token latency. SLOs: initial-token p95 <=250ms; steady-token p95 <=120ms. Streaming p99 allowed higher but must be documented with fallback behavior.
- Client-perceived SLO (optional for contractual SLA): combine server_observed_end_to_end + typical last-mile RTT percentile (use 95th historical from Boreal network). Explicit statement: if client RTT dominates, credit system will exclude last-mile for infra SLA.

POC measurement plan (2-week):
- Week 1: Functional correctness and small-scale latency tuning. Baseline capture of p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and non-streaming using Redwood SDK + custom client instrumenter.
- Week 2: Scale run to 10k concurrent sessions with realistic token distributions, synthetic burst tests (x2), and long-duration stability run (8 hours). Collect server_observed_end_to_end, inference_duration, queue_delay, batch_sizes, token_throughput.
- Artifacts to deliver: load scripts, dashboard (per-route p50/p95/p99), raw traces (Zipkin/Jaeger), sample client SDK logs.

Instrumentation agreement (need sign-off):
- Redwood will emit: request_id, server_ingress_ts, inference_start_ts, inference_end_ts, server_egress_ts, per-token timestamps for streaming.
- Boreal will emit: client_send_ts, client_receive_ts, client_sdk_version, network_region tag.
- Both sides will correlate by request_id. If client clocks unsynced, use server timestamps for contractual SLOs; client metrics used for debugging and UX work.

Capacity & Reserved GPU planning notes:
- Initial reserved pool recommendation: 40 x A100-equivalent GPUs for target throughput with headroom for bursts. (SE estimate; final needs benchmarking).
- Autoscale burst policy desired for radio events; need SLA clause for burst capacity and pricing.
- Warm cache behavior important: first requests after idle show high tail latency; POC must include cache-warmup scenarios and cold-start incidence rate in metrics.

Negotiation / legal items flagged:
- Explicit definition of measurement surface for SLA (server_observed_end_to_end vs client-perceived). Legal will not accept ambiguous timing definitions.
- Remedies table: service credits based on p99 breaches over monthly windows vs token-based refunds. Boreal prefers credits tied to lost revenue estimates—requires Redwood finance to map.

Timeline & recent activity (bulleted):
- 2024-11-06: Intro call (Jordan + Aisha) - high level requirements captured.
- 2024-11-15: Technical deep-dive (SE workshop) - agreed draft SLOs and instrumentation approach (fireflies ff_20241115_01).

- 2024-11-29: Pricing review w/ procurement (shared dedicated quote v3).
- 2024-12-02: SE updated SLO proposal; legal asked for measurement clause revision.

Next steps (short):
- Action A: Redwood SE to deliver final POC load scripts + monitoring dashboard (by 2024-12-06).
- Action B: Legal to align measurement clause: accept server_observed_end_to_end as contract SLO with option to include client-perceived as label-only (target 2024-12-09).
- Action C: Begin POC week of 2024-12-16 pending legal sign-off and reserved capacity scheduling.

Quoted customer notes / direct quote: "We can live with server-side SLOs for contract purposes — but we need a clear way to show the UX impact when last-mile is the culprit."

Short-term risks:
- If measurement definitions remain ambiguous, procurement will not sign reserved capacity until January.
- Cold-starts during peak windows could push p99 beyond acceptable limits; needs explicit warmup guarantees or faster cold-start paths.
